previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, gastroparesis, and recent MSSA bacteremia and C. difficile infection was readmitted one day after discharge for diabetic ketoacidosis. She presented with severe hyperglycemia (glucose 903), anion gap of 19, and epigastric pain, but no vomiting. She was treated in the ICU with an insulin drip, which resolved the DKA within 12 hours. Hemodialysis was performed on two consecutive days for metabolic clearance and fluid management. Persistent hyperglycemia on her prior insulin regimen led to dose adjustments: Lantus increased to 10 units morning and 14 units night, and Humalog modified to include a fixed 4-unit pre-meal dose plus a sliding scale. Her hypertension was managed with increased labetalol, and furosemide was discontinued. She continued antibiotics for MSSA (cefazolin and vancomycin locks) and C. difficile (metronidazole). She remained on her home medications for gastroparesis and was discharged home in stable condition, tolerating a full diet, with detailed instructions on insulin adjustment, medication adherence, and follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ with RUQ pain, abn LFTs  // cholecystitis?

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  liver and gallbladder ultrasound ___

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The hepatic parenchyma appears within normal limits. The contour of the
liver is smooth. There is no focal liver mass. Main portal vein is patent with
hepatopetal flow. There is small ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 3 mm.

GALLBLADDER: There is gallbladder wall thickening. The gallbladder is not
particularly distended and contains sludge. There is no evidence of stones.
There are no other findings to suggest acute cholecystitis.

PANCREAS: Pancreas is not well visualized due to overlying bowel gas.

SPLEEN: Normal echogenicity, measuring 13.3 cm.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Gallbladder wall thickening.  The gallbaldder is not particularly
distended and there are no other findings to suggest acute cholecystitis.

2. Small amount of ascites.

EXAMINATION:  UNILAT UP EXT VEINS US RIGHT

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with RUE AVF, now with extreme pain at site and
hx of MSSA bacteremia. // Eval for abscess or fluid collection

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and Doppler evaluation was performed on the right upper
extremity veins.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

Limited evaluation of the right upper extremity arteriovenous fistula shows
normal, wall-to-wall flow. Of, note the graft was not fully assessed but is
patent.  There is trace edema in the surrounding subcutaneous soft tissues
however no discrete fluid collection is identified.

IMPRESSION: 

Trace edema in the subcutaneous soft tissues of the right upper extremity with
no discrete fluid collection identified. Patent arteriovenous fistula.
